questions.name: Count Digits
questions.description: Given an integer n, count the number of digits in it.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Count Digits" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Repeatedly divide by 10 (or use floor(log10(n)) + 1) and count the steps.
commonMistakes: Forgetting n = 0 has one digit
Using log10 on zero or negatives
followUpQuestions: How do you handle negative numbers?
Can you do it with logarithms safely?

questions.name: Reverse Integer
questions.description: Given a signed 32-bit integer x, return x with its digits reversed, or 0 if the reversed value overflows.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Reverse Integer" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Pop the last digit with x % 10, push it onto the result, and check for overflow before each push.
commonMistakes: Checking overflow after it has already happened
Mishandling the sign of negative numbers
followUpQuestions: How do you detect overflow in a language with 64-bit integers?
What if trailing zeros must be preserved?

questions.name: Palindrome Number
questions.description: Given an integer x, return true if x is a palindrome number.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Palindrome Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Reverse only half of the digits and compare it with the remaining half, so no overflow can occur.
commonMistakes: Converting to a string when constant space is expected
Treating negative numbers as palindromes
followUpQuestions: How would you handle numbers ending in 0?
What changes in a different base?

questions.name: Greatest Common Divisor (Euclid)
questions.description: Given two integers a and b, find their greatest common divisor.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Greatest Common Divisor (Euclid)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use the Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes 0.
commonMistakes: Looping from min(a, b) down to 1 (too slow)
Not handling a zero input
followUpQuestions: How do you compute the LCM from the GCD?
What is the time complexity of Euclid's algorithm?

questions.name: Armstrong Number
questions.description: Check whether a number equals the sum of its digits each raised to the power of the digit count.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Armstrong Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Count the digits first, then sum digit^count over all digits and compare with the original number.
commonMistakes: Using a fixed power of 3 for every number
Modifying the original number and then comparing against it
followUpQuestions: How would you list all Armstrong numbers in a range?
How do you avoid overflow for large inputs?

questions.name: Print All Divisors of a Number
questions.description: Given an integer n, print all of its divisors.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Print All Divisors of a Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Loop i from 1 to sqrt(n); whenever i divides n, record both i and n / i, avoiding duplicates for perfect squares.
commonMistakes: Looping all the way to n instead of sqrt(n)
Printing the square root twice for perfect squares
followUpQuestions: How would you print them in sorted order?
How would you count divisors for many queries?

questions.name: Check for Prime Number
questions.description: Given an integer n, determine whether it is a prime number.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Check for Prime Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: A composite number has a factor no larger than sqrt(n), so test divisors only up to sqrt(n).
commonMistakes: Treating 1 as a prime
Testing divisors up to n instead of sqrt(n)
followUpQuestions: How does the Sieve of Eratosthenes help for many queries?
What is the Miller-Rabin test?

questions.name: Count Primes
questions.description: Given an integer n, return the number of prime numbers strictly less than n.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Count Primes" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes: for each prime p, mark multiples starting from p*p as composite.
commonMistakes: Starting the inner loop at 2*p instead of p*p
Running the outer loop up to n instead of sqrt(n)
followUpQuestions: What is a segmented sieve and when is it needed?
How do you compute the smallest prime factor for every number?

questions.name: Pow(x, n)
questions.description: Implement pow(x, n), which raises x to the integer power n.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Pow(x, n)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use binary exponentiation: square the base and halve the exponent, multiplying into the result when the exponent bit is 1.
commonMistakes: Negating n directly when n is the minimum integer
Looping n times and getting O(n)
followUpQuestions: How do you compute x^n mod m?
Can it be done iteratively?

questions.name: Prime Factorization of a Number
questions.description: Given an integer n, return all of its prime factors.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Prime Factorization of a Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Divide out each factor i from 2 up to sqrt(n); if anything greater than 1 remains, it is itself prime.
commonMistakes: Not dividing repeatedly by the same factor
Forgetting the leftover prime greater than sqrt(n)
followUpQuestions: How do you factorize many numbers quickly with a smallest-prime-factor sieve?
How would you count distinct prime factors?

questions.name: Count Frequency of Array Elements
questions.description: Given an array, count how many times each element appears.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Count Frequency of Array Elements" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Walk the array once and increment a counter for each value in a hash map.
commonMistakes: Using nested loops for O(n^2)
Re-printing an element's count more than once
followUpQuestions: What if values lie in a small range?
How do you find the highest and lowest frequency elements?

questions.name: Highest and Lowest Frequency Element
questions.description: Given an array, find the elements with the highest and lowest frequency.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Highest and Lowest Frequency Element" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Build a frequency map, then scan it once to track the maximum and minimum counts.
commonMistakes: Not defining the tie-breaking rule
Scanning the array again instead of the map
followUpQuestions: How would you return the top k frequent elements?
How do you handle ties?

questions.name: Selection Sort
questions.description: Sort an array by repeatedly selecting the minimum element from the unsorted part and swapping it into place.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Selection Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: For each index i, find the minimum of arr[i..n-1] and swap it with arr[i].
commonMistakes: Swapping when the minimum is already at i
Searching for the minimum from index 0 each time
followUpQuestions: Is selection sort stable?
When is it useful because it minimizes swaps?

questions.name: Bubble Sort
questions.description: Sort an array by repeatedly swapping adjacent elements that are out of order.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Bubble Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: After each pass the largest remaining element bubbles to the end; stop early if no swap happened.
commonMistakes: Not shrinking the inner loop after each pass
Missing the no-swap early exit that gives O(n) on sorted input
followUpQuestions: What is the best-case complexity with the optimization?
Is it stable?

questions.name: Insertion Sort
questions.description: Sort an array by inserting each element into its correct position within the sorted prefix.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Insertion Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Shift larger elements in the sorted prefix one step right, then drop the current element in the gap.
commonMistakes: Swapping repeatedly instead of shifting
Going out of bounds when j drops below 0
followUpQuestions: Why does it perform well on nearly sorted arrays?
How does binary insertion sort help?

questions.name: Merge Sort
questions.description: Sort an array using the divide and conquer approach of merge sort.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Merge Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Split the array in half, recursively sort each half, and merge the two sorted halves with two pointers.
commonMistakes: Allocating a new temporary array at every merge
Wrong mid calculation causing infinite recursion
followUpQuestions: Why is merge sort stable?
How do you sort a linked list with it?

questions.name: Quick Sort
questions.description: Sort an array using quick sort by partitioning around a pivot.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Quick Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Pick a pivot, partition so smaller elements go left and larger go right, then recurse on both sides.
commonMistakes: Always choosing the first element, causing O(n^2) on sorted input
Off-by-one errors in the partition loop
followUpQuestions: How does a random pivot improve the expected case?
How does the Dutch National Flag partition handle duplicates?
questions.timeComplexity: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst

questions.name: Recursive Bubble Sort
questions.description: Implement bubble sort recursively.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Recursive Bubble Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Perform one bubble pass to place the largest element at the end, then recurse on the first n - 1 elements.
commonMistakes: Missing the base case n = 1
Not passing the reduced size into the recursive call
followUpQuestions: What is the recursion depth?
How would you add the no-swap early exit?

questions.name: Recursive Insertion Sort
questions.description: Implement insertion sort recursively.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Recursive Insertion Sort" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Recursively sort the first n - 1 elements, then insert the n-th element into its position.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the base case for size 1
Overwriting the element being inserted
followUpQuestions: How does stack depth compare with the iterative form?
Can you do the insertion step recursively too?

questions.name: Largest Element in an Array
questions.description: Given an array, find its largest element.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Largest Element in an Array" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Keep a running maximum while scanning the array once.
commonMistakes: Initializing the maximum to 0 when all values are negative
Sorting the whole array for no reason
followUpQuestions: How do you find the second largest in one pass?
How do you find it in a stream?

questions.name: Second Largest Element in an Array
questions.description: Given an array, find the second largest distinct element.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Second Largest Element in an Array" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Track the largest and second largest together in one pass, updating both as you go.
commonMistakes: Treating a duplicate of the maximum as the second largest
Initializing both trackers to 0 for negative values
followUpQuestions: How would you find the k-th largest?
How do you handle arrays with fewer than two distinct values?

questions.name: Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated
questions.description: Check whether an array was originally sorted in non-decreasing order and then rotated some number of positions.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Count the places where nums[i] > nums[(i + 1) % n]; a valid array has at most one such drop.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the wrap-around comparison between last and first elements
Rejecting arrays with equal elements
followUpQuestions: How would you find the rotation point?
What if the sort is strictly increasing?

questions.name: Left Rotate Array by One Place
questions.description: Rotate an array to the left by one position.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Left Rotate Array by One Place" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Save the first element, shift every other element one step left, and place the saved element at the end.
commonMistakes: Overwriting the first element before saving it
Allocating a second array unnecessarily
followUpQuestions: How would you rotate by d places?
Why is the reversal method better for large d?

questions.name: Linear Search
questions.description: Given an array and a target, return the index of the target or -1 if absent.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Linear Search" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Walk through the array and return the index at the first match.
commonMistakes: Returning the value instead of the index
Not handling an empty array
followUpQuestions: When is binary search a better option?
How would you return all matching indices?

questions.name: Union of Two Sorted Arrays
questions.description: Given two sorted arrays, return the sorted union of their elements with no duplicates.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Union of Two Sorted Arrays" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use two pointers to merge, skipping a value if it equals the last value added to the result.
commonMistakes: Adding duplicates from the same array
Not draining the remaining elements after one pointer finishes
followUpQuestions: How would you find the intersection instead?
How would the solution change for unsorted arrays?

questions.name: Max Consecutive Ones
questions.description: Given a binary array, return the maximum number of consecutive 1s.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Max Consecutive Ones" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Keep a running count that increments on 1 and resets to 0 on 0, tracking the maximum seen.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to update the maximum at the end of the array
Not resetting the counter on 0
followUpQuestions: How does Max Consecutive Ones III extend this?
What if you may flip one zero?

questions.name: Single Number
questions.description: Every element appears twice except one. Find the element that appears only once.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Single Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: XOR all elements together; pairs cancel out and the unique number remains.
commonMistakes: Using a hash map when O(1) space is required
Not knowing that a ^ a = 0
followUpQuestions: How do you solve Single Number II where others appear three times?
How do you find two unique numbers?

questions.name: Longest Subarray with Sum K (Positives)
questions.description: Given an array of positive integers and a value k, find the length of the longest subarray whose sum equals k.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Longest Subarray with Sum K (Positives)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use a sliding window with two pointers: expand right, and shrink left while the sum exceeds k.
commonMistakes: Using this window approach when negatives are present
Forgetting to shrink the window on overshoot
followUpQuestions: How does the solution change with negative numbers?
How would you count such subarrays?

questions.name: Longest Subarray with Sum K (Positives and Negatives)
questions.description: Given an array that may contain negatives and a value k, find the length of the longest subarray with sum k.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Longest Subarray with Sum K (Positives and Negatives)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Store the first index of each prefix sum in a hash map and look up (prefixSum - k).
commonMistakes: Overwriting the first occurrence of a prefix sum, which shortens the answer
Using sliding window with negatives
followUpQuestions: How would you return the actual subarray?
What if you wanted the shortest one?

questions.name: Print Subarray with Maximum Sum
questions.description: Find the maximum subarray sum and also return the subarray itself.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Print Subarray with Maximum Sum" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Run Kadane's algorithm while remembering the start index where the running sum last restarted.
commonMistakes: Not updating the start index when the sum resets
Returning the wrong end index
followUpQuestions: How do you handle all-negative arrays?
How would you return the first or the shortest such subarray?

questions.name: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
questions.description: Given an equal count of positive and negative integers, rearrange them to alternate signs, starting with positive, preserving relative order.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Rearrange Array Elements by Sign" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Create the result array and place positives at even indices and negatives at odd indices with two write pointers.
commonMistakes: Doing an in-place swap that loses relative order
Mixing up the pointer increments
followUpQuestions: What if the counts of positives and negatives differ?
Can you do it in O(1) extra space?

questions.name: Leaders in an Array
questions.description: Find all elements that are greater than every element to their right.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Leaders in an Array" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Scan from the right while tracking the maximum so far; an element is a leader if it exceeds that maximum.
commonMistakes: Scanning left to right and getting O(n^2)
Not reversing the result to restore order
followUpQuestions: Is the rightmost element always a leader?
How do you count leaders?

questions.name: Majority Element II
questions.description: Find all elements that appear more than floor(n / 3) times.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Majority Element II" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Extend Boyer-Moore with two candidates and two counters, then verify the candidates in a second pass.
commonMistakes: Skipping the verification pass
Allowing the same value to occupy both candidate slots
followUpQuestions: How do you generalize it to n / k?
Why are there at most two such elements?

questions.name: Largest Subarray with Sum 0
questions.description: Given an array, find the length of the longest subarray with sum equal to 0.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Largest Subarray with Sum 0" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Store the first index of each prefix sum; if a prefix sum repeats, the segment between those indices sums to zero.
commonMistakes: Not handling the case when the prefix sum itself is 0
Updating the stored index on every repeat
followUpQuestions: How does this relate to Subarray Sum Equals K?
How would you count such subarrays?

questions.name: Count Subarrays with Given XOR
questions.description: Given an array and a number k, count subarrays whose XOR equals k.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Count Subarrays with Given XOR" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Maintain a running prefix XOR and a frequency map; for each prefix, add the count of (prefix ^ k).
commonMistakes: Forgetting to seed the map with {0: 1}
Mixing XOR with addition in the formula
followUpQuestions: How is this similar to Subarray Sum Equals K?
How would you find the longest such subarray?

questions.name: Find the Repeating and Missing Number
questions.description: An array of size n holds numbers from 1 to n with one number repeated and one missing. Find both.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Find the Repeating and Missing Number" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Compare the sum and sum of squares with the expected values to form two equations, or use XOR splitting.
commonMistakes: Sorting first and paying O(n log n)
Integer overflow when using sums of squares
followUpQuestions: How do you solve it using XOR and a set bit?
What if two numbers are missing?

questions.name: Count Inversions
questions.description: Given an array, count the pairs (i, j) with i < j and arr[i] > arr[j].
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Count Inversions" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use merge sort; while merging, whenever the right element is smaller, add the remaining left-half count.
commonMistakes: Counting inside a nested loop in O(n^2)
Not adding the remaining left elements during a merge
followUpQuestions: How can a Fenwick tree solve it?
How does it relate to measuring array unsortedness?

questions.name: Reverse Pairs
questions.description: Count pairs (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] > 2 * nums[j].
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Reverse Pairs" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Use merge sort and count qualifying pairs with a two-pointer pass before each merge step.
commonMistakes: Merging before counting, which breaks the sorted halves
Overflow when computing 2 * nums[j]
followUpQuestions: How does this differ from standard inversions?
Can a BIT or segment tree solve it?

questions.name: Pascal's Triangle Variations (Row and Element)
questions.description: Given a row index, return that row of Pascal's triangle.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Pascal's Triangle Variations (Row and Element)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Compute each element as C(n, k) using the iterative formula next = prev * (n - k) / (k + 1).
commonMistakes: Computing factorials directly and overflowing
Integer division before multiplication
followUpQuestions: How do you get a single element C(r, c)?
Can you build the row with O(k) space?

questions.name: Rotate Array by D Places (Left)
questions.description: Rotate an array to the left by d positions.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Rotate Array by D Places (Left)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Reverse the first d elements, reverse the rest, then reverse the whole array.
commonMistakes: Not reducing d modulo n
Using extra memory when in-place is possible
followUpQuestions: How do you rotate right instead?
What is the cyclic replacement method?

questions.name: Remove Outermost Parentheses
questions.description: Remove the outermost parentheses of every primitive part of a valid parentheses string.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Remove Outermost Parentheses" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Track depth with a counter; add a character only if it is not an outermost opening or closing parenthesis.
commonMistakes: Updating depth in the wrong order relative to the check
Using a stack when a counter suffices
followUpQuestions: How would you do it with a stack?
How do you count the primitive parts?

questions.name: Reverse Words in a String
questions.description: Given a string, reverse the order of its words, trimming extra spaces.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Reverse Words in a String" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Split by whitespace, reverse the words, and join with a single space (or reverse in place).
commonMistakes: Leaving extra spaces in the result
Reversing characters instead of words
followUpQuestions: How do you do it in place with O(1) space?
What if punctuation attaches to words?

questions.name: Largest Odd Number in String
questions.description: Given a numeric string, return the largest-valued odd number that is a substring, or an empty string.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Largest Odd Number in String" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Scan from the right for the first odd digit and return the prefix ending at it.
commonMistakes: Converting the string to an integer and overflowing
Returning the rightmost odd digit alone
followUpQuestions: Why does the rightmost odd digit give the answer?
How would you return the largest even number?

questions.name: Longest Common Prefix
questions.description: Find the longest common prefix among an array of strings.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Longest Common Prefix" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Take the first string as the prefix and shorten it until every other string starts with it.
commonMistakes: Not handling an empty array
Indexing past the end of a shorter string
followUpQuestions: How does sorting reduce the comparison to first and last strings?
How would a trie solve it?

questions.name: Rotate String
questions.description: Check whether string goal can be obtained by rotating string s some number of times.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Rotate String" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: If goal is a rotation of s, it must appear inside s + s with equal lengths.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to compare lengths first
Checking rotations one by one in O(n^2)
followUpQuestions: How does KMP make the substring search linear?
How would you find the rotation amount?

questions.name: Sort Characters By Frequency
questions.description: Sort a string in decreasing order based on character frequency.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Sort Characters By Frequency" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Count frequencies with a hash map, then sort or bucket the characters by count and rebuild the string.
commonMistakes: Emitting each character only once
Not grouping equal characters together
followUpQuestions: How does bucket sort achieve O(n)?
How would you break ties alphabetically?

questions.name: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
questions.description: Return the maximum nesting depth of parentheses in a valid expression string.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Increment a counter on '(' and decrement on ')', tracking the maximum value reached.
commonMistakes: Decrementing before recording the maximum
Counting other characters
followUpQuestions: How would you validate the expression too?
How do you handle multiple bracket types?

questions.name: Roman to Integer
questions.description: Convert a Roman numeral string to an integer.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Roman to Integer" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Map symbols to values; subtract a value if a larger symbol follows it, otherwise add it.
commonMistakes: Not handling subtractive pairs like IV and IX
Reading past the end when checking the next symbol
followUpQuestions: How would you convert integer to Roman?
How would you validate a Roman numeral?

questions.name: String to Integer (atoi)
questions.description: Implement atoi, which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "String to Integer (atoi)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Skip whitespace, read an optional sign, accumulate digits, and clamp the value on overflow.
commonMistakes: Checking overflow after it has happened
Not stopping at the first non-digit character
followUpQuestions: How do you detect overflow without a bigger type?
How would you extend it to other bases?

questions.name: Count Number of Substrings (Sum of Beauty)
questions.description: Return the sum of the beauty (max frequency minus min frequency) over all substrings of a string.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Count Number of Substrings (Sum of Beauty)" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Fix a start index, extend the end while updating a 26-slot frequency array, and compute beauty from it.
commonMistakes: Counting characters with zero frequency in the minimum
Recomputing frequencies from scratch
followUpQuestions: Can you do it faster than O(26 * n^2)?
How would you apply it to a stream?

questions.name: Binary Search
questions.description: Given a sorted array and a target, return the index of the target or -1.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Binary Search" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Compare the middle element with the target and discard half of the range each iteration.
commonMistakes: Computing mid as (lo + hi) / 2 and overflowing
Infinite loops from wrong bound updates
followUpQuestions: How do you implement it recursively?
Why does mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 matter?

questions.name: Lower Bound
questions.description: Find the first index in a sorted array whose value is greater than or equal to x.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Lower Bound" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Binary search while keeping a candidate answer; when arr[mid] >= x, record it and search left.
commonMistakes: Returning mid without tracking the candidate
Returning -1 instead of n when none qualifies
followUpQuestions: How does it differ from upper bound?
How is it used for counting occurrences?

questions.name: Upper Bound
questions.description: Find the first index in a sorted array whose value is strictly greater than x.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Upper Bound" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: Binary search with the condition arr[mid] > x; record the candidate and move left, otherwise move right.
commonMistakes: Using >= instead of >
Not returning n when no element exceeds x
followUpQuestions: How do upper and lower bound give a count of x?
What changes for descending arrays?

questions.name: Search Insert Position
questions.description: Return the index of the target in a sorted array, or where it would be inserted to keep order.
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Search Insert Position" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
questions.hint: This is the lower bound of the target: the first index with value >= target.
commonMistakes: Returning -1 when the target is missing
Wrong boundary updates
followUpQuestions: How does it change with duplicates?
How would you insert into a rotated array?

questions.name: Floor and Ceil in Sorted Array
questions.description: Given a sorted array and x, find the floor (largest value <= x) and ceil (smallest value >= x).
questions.interviewQuestion: How would you solve "Floor and Ceil in Sorted Array" optimally, and what is the time and space complexity of your approach?
